cards.designTerms: The Game record should own the claimed-token fact and derive it from the transactions; Delivery is the one seam a claim crosses to reach a screen, and each tablet is a Screens adapter that draws it. Today the tablet's networked storage module updates its copy through one hand-wired handler per message, so the seam leaks: any path without a handler leaves the copy stale. No locality.
cards.standaloneLine: In a standalone game: one GM tablet holds the only copy, so tablets cannot drift, but it refreshes screens only on wired events. Two standalone tablets are two separate games; one tablet per game is undecided. Under candidate A the tablet hosts the same Game record and Lifecycle; under B its own engine, kept equal by tests.
cards.shapeChange: The card's candidate let every tablet keep a claim list and replace it by one function. The map puts claims in the Game record alone, derived from the transactions, with Delivery carrying the fact and Lifecycle telling the boundary. A tablet draws what it is delivered and asks at each tap, so a delete or a reset cannot leave a stale list anywhere.

Equipment's state arrives dated, the Verdict calls a failed profile no-go, not no equipment, and one liveness rule says the engine is gone. Screens draws unknown, old and down as such. The card's first design, in Delivery. Or: each job delivers its own facts under a shared envelope.

cards.designTerms: Delivery should own the label every fact carries (what it is, how old, how sure), fed by Equipment's dated state and the Verdict's paper-or-live words; Screens draws the label at that seam. Today the pushed facts' interface carries neither status nor age, so snapshot builders turn errors into defaults and the seam leaks: a failure crosses as a normal value.
cards.standaloneLine: In a standalone game: the missing engine draws as an outage: the phone says Offline all night, the ESP32 shows red Disconnected, a rising queue, a video token says Rescan later. Nothing says standalone by choice; no readiness verdict exists. The shape gives both: a declared standalone fact every device reads and, under candidate A, the tablet's own Verdict.
cards.shapeChange: The card made the health registry the owner of known, unknown and stale. The map makes the label part of every delivered fact in Delivery, with Equipment dating its picture, the Verdict reporting a failed profile as a no-go, and one liveness rule from Connections and roles, so the TV clock and the music card draw old or down the same way the health panel does.
